title: API: entity-definition CRUD + GET /retrieve/tools + POST /retrieve/:entity

epic.name: Context Retriever (entity-schema -> auto-generated agent tool surface)

priority_note: Exposes entity management + the generated tool list + the query executor over HTTP (the MCP layer is a thin client). Depends on the executor (30.3).

background.reference: GitHub issue #309; extends the :authenticated pipeline. Agent-native: entity definitions are managed via API/MCP, NOT a LiveView (the #309 entity-designer LiveView is dropped — no web UI).
background.includes: US-30.1/30.2/30.3 provide the registry, generator, and executor. This story wires them to HTTP: CRUD for entity definitions, a per-tenant generated-tool-spec listing, and the generic query-execution endpoint.

story.as_a: a tenant admin (via API) and an agent
story.i_want_to: create/read/update/delete my entity definitions, list the generated tool specs for my tenant, and execute a generated query
story.so_that: the structured-data tool surface is defined and used over the same governed transport as knowledge and memory

rationale: Putting entity CRUD, the generated-tool listing, and the executor behind /api/v1 on the existing authenticated/witness pipeline is what lets the MCP server stay a thin client and inherit tenant resolution + role gating. It also delivers the entity-definition management that the dropped LiveView would have provided, agent-natively.

acceptance_criteria.description: LoopctlWeb.ContextRetrieverController on the :authenticated pipeline: CRUD for entity definitions (POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/entities), GET /api/v1/retrieve/tools (generated tool specs for the tenant), POST /api/v1/retrieve/:entity (execute via the Executor). Scope from the resolved key; body tenant ignored.

Role gating: defining/mutating entity definitions requires >= user role (403 for agent/orchestrator). Querying (/retrieve/*) requires only authentication — agent is the FLOOR role (superadmin>user>orchestrator>agent), so every authenticated key may query; the negative case is 401 unauthenticated, NOT a 'below-agent 403' (no such role exists). Reuse Loopctl.Auth.Role + the full authenticated/witness/custody chain.
The model-invoked /retrieve/:entity endpoint is rate-limited per tenant (reuse Loopctl.RateLimiter.Hammer as elsewhere) so a looping/hostile agent cannot flood the executor; over-limit returns 429.
GET /api/v1/retrieve/tools returns only the calling tenant's generated specs (from ToolGenerator over Registry.for_tenant); another tenant's entities never appear.

POST /api/v1/retrieve/:entity validates the entity + field/operation against the tenant's definitions, calls Executor.run, and returns %{results, meta}; a request for an unknown entity or non-allowlisted field is 4xx, not executed.
OpenAPI: operation macros in the controller (schemas under lib/loopctl/api_spec/); endpoints render at /swaggerui and openapi_test passes.

test_cases.name: define an entity then list + query it
expected_results: entity created; tools list includes cr_filter_project_by_status; query returns tenant's active projects with meta

test_cases.name: agent cannot define entities; unauthenticated cannot query
expected_results: define is 403 for agent (below user); query with no valid key is 401 (agent is the floor role, so any authenticated key may query — there is no below-agent role to 403)

test_cases.name: entity update + delete regenerate the tool surface
steps: PATCH /api/v1/entities/:id (mark a new field filterable) as user_key
expected_results: after PATCH the generated tools reflect the new field; after DELETE the entity's tools are gone

test_cases.name: /retrieve is rate-limited
preconditions: a tenant at its /retrieve rate limit

test_cases.name: tools + queries never cross tenant
preconditions: tenant_u = fixture(:tenant); {_, key_u} = fixture(:api_key, tenant: tenant_u, role: :agent)
expected_results: key_u sees none of tenant_t's tools; the query for tenant_t's entity is unknown/4xx for key_u — never returns tenant_t rows

technical_notes: NO LiveView (agent-native); entity CRUD replaces the dropped #309 entity-designer UI.
Role gating via Loopctl.Auth.Role (define >= user, query >= agent); reuse the existing pipeline + error envelope.
OpenAPI operation macros in the controller; schemas in lib/loopctl/api_spec/.
